purpose: Week 9 evidence: the actual JSON-RPC frames exchanged over stdio between an MCP client and each configured server.

source_of_truth.method: A recording stdio proxy (a passive byte tap) was inserted between the official MCP Python client and each real server. The client connected to the proxy; the proxy spawned the real server command and forwarded every frame byte-for-byte in both directions, recording the exact bytes as they crossed.
source_of_truth.guarantee: Every 'raw' string below is the verbatim frame as transmitted. No frame was written, edited, normalized or reconstructed by hand.
source_of_truth.frame_source: recorded by the proxy while the official client (mcp Python SDK) drove a normal session
source_of_truth.stderr_note: Child stderr (startup banners, HF hub logs, library prints) was inherited by the proxy and deliberately NOT recorded as protocol messages. Only stdout JSON-RPC frames appear below.
source_of_truth.secrets_note: No environment variables are included beyond the non-secret DOC_SEARCH_* keys in mcp_config.json. No API keys or .env values were captured.

jsonrpc.value_observed: the 2.0 JSON-RPC specification version string, identical in every frame
jsonrpc.meaning: Protocol version of the message format itself. Always present on requests, responses and notifications.

id.value_observed: integer 0, 1, 2 in this capture (chosen by the client, echoed by the server)
id.meaning: Correlation identifier. Present on requests and responses; absent on notifications.

method.meaning: The operation name. Present on requests and notifications, absent on responses.

params.meaning: Arguments for the request's method. Present on requests, absent on responses.

result.value_observed: the payload returned by the server on success
result.meaning: Successful response payload. Present on a success response, replaced by 'error' on failure.

error.value_observed: absent from every frame in this capture
error.meaning: Failure payload, carrying a numeric code and message. Replaces 'result' on a failed request. No error frames were recorded: all three requests per server succeeded.

message_type_annotations.request: Client to server. Carries 'method' and 'id'; expects exactly one matching response with the same 'id'.
message_type_annotations.notification: Client to server, no 'id'. Fire-and-forget; the server must not reply. Used to confirm that initialization finished.
message_type_annotations.response: Server to client. Carries the 'id' of the request it answers plus 'result' (success) or 'error' (failure).

critical_distinction.explanation: The figure 20 is the ARITHMETIC SUM of two independent stdio servers. It is not a tool list that any single session in this evidence exposed. Each server runs as its own OS process with its own stdin/stdout pair, and MCP has no cross-server aggregation. In this capture the doc-search session exposed exactly 4 tools and the package-registry session exposed exactly 16 tools; no session saw all 20. A host application that loads both servers from mcp_config.json would present all 20 tools to its model in one session, but that combined view was NOT captured or verified here.

llm_location.principle: MCP is the tool-communication protocol, not the model. MCP standardises how a host discovers and invokes tools (JSON-RPC over stdio/HTTP). It says nothing about which model reasons, and an MCP server can be, and here is, a plain deterministic process with no model in it at all.

doc_search_tool_chain: -> app/services/hybrid_retrieval.py:42 _bm25_rank (hand-rolled Okapi BM25, stdlib math only)
why_the_mcp_servers_hold_no_llm.embedding_model_is_not_an_llm: app/services/embedder.py:20 imports SentenceTransformer and embedder.py:58 calls .encode(), producing 384-dim float vectors (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, app/core/config.py:34). There is no prompt, no chat template, no sampling and no token decoding in that file. It is a bi-encoder used for cosine similarity, so it performs no generative inference and is not an LLM.
why_the_mcp_servers_hold_no_llm.no_llm_reranking: Ranking is dense cosine + BM25 fused positionally by RRF. tools/reference_search.py:93 computes 'relevance' arithmetically from the vector distance. Nothing in the chain asks a model to rerank, rewrite or summarise. Both MCP servers are deterministic processes.
why_the_mcp_servers_hold_no_llm.verification_method: repo-wide grep for llm|gemini|groq|generate_answer across E:\week3\tools\ returned no matches; the only generator call sites in the repo are the two in app/services/llm_provider.py plus scripts/replay_trace.py:152-171, which is a standalone diagnostic not on any server path

offline_path.effect: agent/agent_loop.py:341 routes to the deterministic OfflineReasoner.decide() and the live branch at :358 that would call llm_call is never reached, so no LLM runs at all; workflow/deterministic_workflow.py:114-120 returns a fixed string
offline_path.answer_source: eval/offline_answers.py:60 synthesize_grounded_answer returns the highest-scoring fact-bearing sentence verbatim by regex/lexical scoring, not generation

llm_location.conclusion: The model runs in the host application's own process (app/services/llm_provider.py, reached from agent/agent_loop.py and the FastAPI routes), never inside an MCP server. The two servers captured here are deterministic tool providers over ChromaDB and public package registries.

limitations: Only the stdio transport was captured. HTTP/SSE transports were not exercised.
The capture is a single successful session per server. Error handling, timeouts, cancellation and tool-list-changed notifications were not exercised, so no 'error' frames exist in this evidence.

Timings (t_ms) are wall-clock from proxy start and include one-off startup cost: doc-search's first response took ~32s because the server loads chromadb and sentence-transformers at import. Later sessions were much faster.
doc-search exposes tools/listChanged=false while package-registry exposes listChanged=true; the tools/list_changed notification was not observed from either server within this capture window.
The 20-tool figure is a sum over two processes. No single MCP session in this evidence exposed a combined 20-tool list, so that combined view remains unverified.

package-registry reached public registries over the network; results (for example react 19.3.0) reflect the registry state at capture time and will change. Its Cargo tools returned HTTP 403 from crates.io in a separate earlier probe, so those tools may be unreliable from this network.
This proxy had to resolve the Windows shim npx to npx.cmd because subprocess.Popen does not apply PATHEXT; a host that does not do this will fail to start the package-registry server.
